causes.text: On 2024-06-18, Reuters reported U.S. farm incomes were forecast to plunge about 25% in 2024 as commodity prices slumped while government support faded and borrowing and labor costs rose; farmers were cutting spending and rural economies were feeling the pain.

source_info.title: Farmers' financial pain spills from Kansas wheat fields to Main Streets

causes.text: On 2024-07-31, CNH Industrial cut its 2024 profit forecast, citing slower demand for tractors and combines; it guided agriculture segment sales to fall 15-20% amid falling crop prices and rising production costs.

source_info.title: CNH Industrial lowers profit forecast on slow demand for farming products

effects.text: On 2024-11-21, Deere beat earnings expectations as lower production costs cushioned weak demand; despite a cautious 2025 outlook, shares rose about 8% that day.

source_info.title: Deere's profit beat overshadows tepid 2025 outlook, shares rise

causal_reasoning_chain.description: In June 2024, U.S. farm incomes were forecast to plunge about 25% due to lower commodity prices, fading government support, and higher financing and labor costs; farmers reduced spending and rural communities felt the squeeze.
In late July 2024, CNH Industrial lowered its 2024 profit forecast and signaled agriculture segment sales would drop 15-20%, reinforcing expectations of a prolonged downturn in farm equipment demand.

On 2024-11-21, Deere reported a profit beat as cost reductions offset soft demand; despite a cautious 2025 outlook, investors-primed by months of weak industry signals-saw the results as resilient and pushed the stock up about 8% that day.

rationale: A sharp deterioration in farm incomes and a competitor's forecast cut signaled weak demand heading into Deere's release. Because expectations were low, Deere's cost-driven beat produced a positive surprise and a relief rally.
counterfactual_analysis: If farm incomes had not fallen and CNH had not issued a forecast cut, investors might have expected stronger growth from Deere and reacted less positively to a cautious outlook; conversely, with healthier farm economics, Deere might have guided more bullishly.

adversarial_confounders.text: Deere's internal efficiency improvements and pricing strategies.
adversarial_confounders.impact: Cost controls and price discipline may have driven the earnings beat independent of macro conditions and competitor signals.

adversarial_confounders.text: Foreign exchange movements and geopolitical tensions.
adversarial_confounders.impact: Currency swings or trade barriers could move profits and sentiment separately from farm incomes or competitor guidance.

details.pestel_factor: Economic - Falling commodity prices and high borrowing costs
details.commentary: Falling commodity prices, tighter credit and rising operating costs created a tough economic backdrop for farmers and equipment makers. These conditions depressed sector demand, making Deere's ability to cut production costs and still beat earnings expectations more notable to investors.

Signals of weaker farm income and CNH Industrial's profit warning encouraged Deere to trim production and manage costs ahead of the downturn. When demand softened but costs fell even faster, the earnings beat and share-price jump showed a balancing response that partially offset macro headwinds.
